title: Rowshape Fixture
description: A rowshape.yaml fixture, format version "1" (RFC-0001). A fixture contains no rows from a database — only statistics computed from them, each carrying the confidence it is known at. Unknown fields are ignored by readers (RFC §12); x_-prefixed keys are reserved for vendor extensions.

rowshape_fixture.description: Format version. A reader understands a whole major: it accepts "1" and any minor within it ("1.4") and MUST refuse a different major (RFC §12).

types.description: Qualified user-defined type name (schema.type), exactly as it appears in a column's `type`, -> its definition (RFC-0001 §6.7). Optional: a fixture whose columns use only built-in types omits it.

extensions.description: Extension name -> what the consumer needs to install it (RFC-0001 §6.8). Only the extensions the read schema actually references, resolved from column types and index operator classes — never every extension merely installed on the source. Optional: a schema using no extensions omits it.

confidence.description: The confidence a fact is known at, strictly ordered exact > measured > estimated > declared (RFC §7.1).

version.description: Engine major version — mandatory, because cost models are engine-version-conditional (RFC §9.1).

intFact.description: An integer fact, as a {value, confidence, via} object or a bare scalar (shorthand for confidence:estimated, RFC §6.1).

uniqueFact.description: Uniqueness. It MUST be exact or absent — a sample can never establish it (RFC §7.2). As an object, confidence is constrained to exact.

identity.description: Whether an identity column is GENERATED ALWAYS or BY DEFAULT (RFC-0001 §6.1). An ALWAYS column rejects an explicit value in an INSERT unless the statement says OVERRIDING SYSTEM VALUE, so the two are not interchangeable. Absent means by_default, the permissive reading.

generated_expression.description: A STORED generated column's expression, verbatim (RFC-0001 §6.1). The literal string "opaque" under privacy:strict; a consumer MUST NOT invent a replacement, which would compute values production never held.

default.description: The column's DEFAULT expression, verbatim (RFC-0001 §6.1). It is what makes a NOT NULL column insertable without naming it; a consumer that drops it produces a target that rejects ordinary inserts production accepts. A nextval(...) default obliges the consumer to create that sequence. The literal string "opaque" under privacy:strict; a generated or identity column MUST NOT record one.

allOf.title: RFC §6.1 — no range on text/bytea
allOf.description: A text or bytea column MUST NOT carry a range: its min and max would be REAL PRODUCTION VALUES, which is exactly what a fixture must never contain (INV-NO-ROWS). Numeric and temporal ranges are bounds; text ranges are data. Enforced here as well as in the Go conformance suite so a third-party emitter validating against the published schema alone cannot emit an invalid fixture.

then.$comment: range is forbidden on this type

userType.description: An enum or domain a column is typed with (RFC-0001 §6.7). A column's `type` is only a name; without a definition a consumer cannot recreate the type.

kind.description: Which kind of user-defined type this is.

labels.description: An enum's full vocabulary in DECLARATION ORDER, which is normative: engines order an enum by it. Withheld under privacy:strict.

label_count.description: Number of enum labels. Present even when `labels` is withheld, because cardinality is shape: a consumer can still build a type of the right size.

base.description: A domain's underlying type, itself possibly another domain (resolved transitively).

not_null.description: A domain declared NOT NULL, which constrains every column using it.

check.description: A domain's constraint expression over the keyword VALUE, verbatim. The literal string "opaque" under privacy:strict; a consumer MUST NOT invent a replacement predicate.

extension.description: An engine extension the read schema depends on (RFC-0001 §6.8). §6.7 covers a type the database defines; this covers one that arrives with an extension and cannot be reconstructed from the catalog — a `citext` column names a type a fresh disposable database has never heard of. No version is recorded: the claim is that the schema needs citext, not a particular citext.

schema.description: Where the extension's objects live. It matters because a type name in a column can be schema-qualified: `ext.citext` and `public.citext` are different strings and only one resolves.
